battle.title: Table Builder Brawl
battle.description: Fill the DP table bottom-up and out-think greedy traps.

options: Recurse from the full problem and cache results on the way down
Solve the smallest subproblems first and fill a table iteratively up to the answer
Try all combinations and keep the best one
Split the input in half and merge the answers
questions.answer: Solve the smallest subproblems first and fill a table iteratively up to the answer
questions.explanation: Tabulation uses loops in an order where each cell's dependencies are already filled. Recursing with a cache is top-down memoization instead.

questions.text: This DP finds the minimum number of coins for an amount. What does it print?
questions.explanation: dp[6] = 2 using 3 + 3. A greedy choice (take the biggest coin 4, then 1 + 1) needs 3 coins, which is the tempting wrong answer.

questions.text: You need the minimum coins for an amount of 1000000, and a recursive memoized solution would nest a million calls deep. Which is safer?
options: The same recursion but with a bigger memo array
A bottom-up table filled with a loop from 0 up to the amount
A greedy algorithm that always takes the largest coin
questions.answer: A bottom-up table filled with a loop from 0 up to the amount
questions.explanation: A loop has no deep call stack, so it cannot overflow, and it still does O(amount * coins) work. A larger memo does not shorten the recursion depth and greedy is not correct for every coin set.

questions.text: For min-coin change with an amount A and k coin values, what are the time and space of the standard tabulation?
questions.explanation: There are A + 1 table cells and each tries k coins. The exponential bound belongs to brute-force recursion without a table.

questions.text: This table computes the length of the longest common subsequence of ABCBD and BDCB. What does it print?
questions.explanation: One longest common subsequence is B, C, B (length 3): it appears in order in both strings. 4 would need a common subsequence like BDCB, but ABCBD has no D before C and B.

coding.title: Fewest Coins
coding.description: You have an unlimited supply of coins of the given denominations. Find the minimum number of coins needed to make exactly the target amount, or print -1 if it cannot be made. An amount of 0 needs 0 coins. Greedy choices fail for some coin sets, so build a DP table.
coding.inputDescription: Line 1: n (number of denominations) and the amount. Line 2: n positive integers (the coin values).
coding.outputDescription: A single integer: the minimum number of coins, or -1.
